    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

234	    # comparison; no underlying json/hashlib exception is ever surfaced
235	    # (everything here is type/shape checked by hand). The manifest itself

238	    # object back.
239	    if not isinstance(manifest, dict) or set(manifest) != _MANIFEST_KEYS:
240	        raise ValueError(

242	            "'version', 'byte_length', 'byte_sha256' and 'tenants', got "
243	            f"{manifest!r}"

247	            or version != MANIFEST_VERSION:

250	        )
251	    byte_length = manifest["byte_length"]

256	        )

262	            f"{type(tenants).__name__}"
263	        )

265	    for entry in tenants:

267	                or set(entry) != _MANIFEST_TENANT_KEYS:
268	            raise ValueError(
269	                "each manifest tenant must be an object containing exactly "
270	                "the keys 'tenant', 'count' and 'hash', got "
271	                f"{entry!r}"
272	            )

277	            raise ValueError(

279	            )

281	        key = AuditChain._tenant_key(tenant)
282	        if key in seen:
283	            raise ValueError(
284	                "duplicate tenant in manifest (same canonical JSON identity): "
285	                f"{tenant!r}"
286	            )
287	        seen.add(key)

356	class _StreamScan:
357	    # Internal incremental engine behind the single-consumption streaming
358	    # entry points (verify_stream, verify_all_stream, heads_stream and
359	    # manifest_stream). The history arrives as an ordered iterable of bytes
360	    # chunks and is validated one chunk at a time, so the caller never has to
361	    # assemble the full bytes: chunks may be cut at any byte boundary
362	    # (mid-UTF-8-sequence, mid-JSON-object or mid-LF), empty chunks are
363	    # allowed, and only the chunks' in-order concatenation is the history.
364	    #
365	    # The verdict nevertheless matches the in-memory entry points for that
366	    # concatenation field for field, because every physical line is rebuilt
367	    # and handed to the same strict decoder and the same tenant/seq/prev/hash
368	    # checks in the same physical order:
369	    #   * physical lines are bounded by exactly one character, the byte 0x0A
370	    #     (LF); a trailing CR stays attached to its line the way _split_lf
371	    #     keeps it, and the empty segment after a final LF is not an extra
372	    #     line (empty buffer at end() yields nothing);
373	    #   * a line's bytes are UTF-8 decoded only once its LF arrives (or at
374	    #     end() for the final LF-less tail), so a multibyte sequence split
375	    #     across chunks is rebuilt before decoding while the first illegal
376	    #     byte is reported on its own physical line -- one plus the number of
377	    #     LFs already processed -- the same bad_line _decode_lines locates;
378	    #   * a completed line is parsed the instant its LF arrives, so the first
379	    #     defective line stops the scan and the streaming entry points never
380	    #     pull another chunk; a valid history is consumed to the end.
381	    #
382	    # all_tenants=False runs verify_bytes' single-tenant scan (records of
383	    # other canonical identities interleave freely and are skipped) and a
384	    # defect is kept as (reason, at), "at" being the expected seq or the
385	    # physical line exactly as _verify_snapshot fills it. all_tenants=True
386	    # runs verify_all_bytes' physical-order scan over every tenant and keeps
387	    # (reason, line, tenant, state_seq): line/tenant/reason back the
388	    # verify_all/heads failure object and state_seq fills the AuditChainStateError
389	    # seq exactly the way _scan_all_chains fills it for manifest_bytes
390	    # (None/None on a line that cannot name a tenant; the record's own seq
391	    # when present as a plain int on a missing-field line, else the expected
392	    # seq). The running byte count and whole-stream sha256 back manifest.
393	    def __init__(self, chain, all_tenants, tenant=None):
394	        self._chain = chain
395	        self._all_tenants = all_tenants
396	        # Single-tenant mode state.
397	        self._key = chain._tenant_key(tenant) if not all_tenants else None
398	        self._expected = 1
399	        self._prev = ZERO
400	        self.count = 0
401	        # All-tenant state: serialized key -> [expected_seq, prev_hash, count]
402	        # and (original_tenant, state) in first-appearance order.
403	        self._states = {}
404	        self._order = []
405	        # Stream mechanics: pending bytes after the last processed LF, the
406	        # completed physical-line count, total consumed bytes, the whole-input
407	        # digest and the first defect reported (None while valid).
408	        self._buffer = b""
409	        self._line_no = 0
410	        self._byte_length = 0
411	        self._hasher = hashlib.sha256()
412	        self._defect = None
413	
414	    @property
415	    def byte_length(self):
416	        return self._byte_length
417	
418	    def feed(self, chunk):
419	        # Fold one bytes chunk into the running stream and validate every
420	        # physical line it completes. Returns the first defect tuple (kept for
421	        # end()) or None while the history stays valid. Bytes are accounted
422	        # for before line validation, which only matters for a successful
423	        # manifest (a defect discards the counters anyway).
424	        if self._defect is not None:
425	            return self._defect
426	        self._byte_length += len(chunk)
427	        self._hasher.update(chunk)
428	        self._buffer += chunk
429	        while True:
430	            idx = self._buffer.find(b"\n")
431	            if idx < 0:
432	                return None
433	            line_bytes = self._buffer[:idx]
434	            self._buffer = self._buffer[idx + 1:]
435	            self._line_no += 1
436	            defect = self._check_line(line_bytes)
437	            if defect is not None:
438	                self._defect = defect
439	                return defect
440	
441	    def end(self):
442	        # Finalize the stream: the bytes still pending after the last LF are
443	        # the final physical line (a history need not end with LF). Returns
444	        # the first defect tuple or None for a fully valid history.
445	        if self._defect is not None:
446	            return self._defect
447	        if self._buffer:
448	            self._line_no += 1
449	            defect = self._check_line(self._buffer)
450	            self._buffer = b""
451	            if defect is not None:
452	                self._defect = defect
453	        return self._defect
454	
455	    def _check_line(self, line_bytes):
456	        # Validate one complete physical line. Strict UTF-8 decoding happens
457	        # here on the line's exact bytes (a split multibyte sequence has been
458	        # rebuilt by feed), then strict standard JSON; neither underlying
459	        # exception ever escapes. The first undecodable/unparseable line is a
460	        # missing-class defect with no determinable tenant.
461	        try:
462	            raw = line_bytes.decode("utf-8")
463	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
464	            return self._bad_line()
465	        try:
466	            item = _strict_loads(raw)
467	        except Exception:
468	            return self._bad_line()
469	        if self._all_tenants:
470	            return self._check_all_item(item)
471	        return self._check_tenant_item(item)
472	
473	    def _bad_line(self):
474	        if self._all_tenants:
475	            return ("missing", self._line_no, None, None)
476	        return ("missing", self._line_no)
477	
478	    def _check_tenant_item(self, item):
479	        # Single-tenant scan, line for line the rules _scan applies: foreign
480	        # canonical identities are skipped, a target record's fields/seq/
481	        # prev/hash are checked from (1, ZERO), and a missing-field defect
482	        # carries the record's own seq when it is a plain int so _verify_snapshot
483	        # reports that seq, else the physical line.
484	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:
485	            return ("missing", self._line_no)
486	        if self._chain._tenant_key(item["tenant"]) != self._key:
487	            return None
488	        if any(k not in item for k in FIELDS):
489	            seq = item.get("seq")
490	            at = seq if isinstance(seq, int) and not isinstance(seq, bool) \
491	                else self._line_no
492	            return ("missing", at)
493	        seq = item["seq"]
494	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int) \
495	                or seq != self._expected:
496	            return ("sequence", self._expected)
497	        if item["prev"] != self._prev:
498	            return ("digest", self._expected)
499	        if item["hash"] != self._chain._hash(item):
500	            return ("digest", self._expected)
501	        self.count += 1
502	        self._prev = item["hash"]
503	        self._expected += 1
504	        return None
505	
506	    def _check_all_item(self, item):
507	        # Every-tenant physical-order scan, line for line the rules
508	        # _verify_all_snapshot and _scan_all_chains share. The state is looked
509	        # up before the field check, so a missing-field line fills the
510	        # manifest state error's seq with its own plain-int seq or the
511	        # expected one, exactly _scan_all_chains' rule; the verify_all/heads
512	        # failure object instead reports the physical line as "at".
513	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:
514	            return ("missing", self._line_no, None, None)
515	        tenant = item["tenant"]
516	        key = self._chain._tenant_key(tenant)
517	        state = self._states.get(key)
518	        if state is None:
519	            state = [1, ZERO, 0]
520	            self._states[key] = state
521	            self._order.append((tenant, state))
522	        expected, _prev, _count = state
523	        if any(k not in item for k in FIELDS):
524	            seq = item.get("seq")
525	            state_seq = seq if isinstance(seq, int) \
526	                and not isinstance(seq, bool) else expected
527	            return ("missing", self._line_no, tenant, state_seq)
528	        seq = item["seq"]
529	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int) \
530	                or seq != expected:
531	            return ("sequence", self._line_no, tenant, expected)
532	        if item["prev"] != state[1]:
533	            return ("digest", self._line_no, tenant, expected)
534	        if item["hash"] != self._chain._hash(item):
535	            return ("digest", self._line_no, tenant, expected)
536	        state[0] += 1
537	        state[1] = item["hash"]
538	        state[2] += 1
539	        return None
540	
541	    def verify_all_result(self, with_hash=False):
542	        # Project the successful scan into verify_all_bytes' result shape
543	        # (with_hash=True adds each tenant's verified tail hash for heads).
544	        tenants = []
545	        for tenant, state in self._order:
546	            entry = {"tenant": tenant, "count": state[2]}
547	            if with_hash:
548	                entry["hash"] = state[1]
549	            tenants.append(entry)
550	        return {"ok": True, "tenants": tenants}
551	
552	    def manifest_result(self):
553	        # Project the successful stream into the version-1 manifest: the
554	        # byte length and sha256 describe the exact concatenated input bytes
555	        # and tenants follow physical first-appearance order with original
556	        # tenant value, verified count and last-record hash.
557	        return {
558	            "version": MANIFEST_VERSION,
559	            "byte_length": self._byte_length,
560	            "byte_sha256": self._hasher.hexdigest(),
561	            "tenants": [
562	                {"tenant": tenant, "count": state[2], "hash": state[1]}
563	                for tenant, state in self._order
564	            ],
565	        }

568	class _TenantRangeScan:
569	    # Internal incremental engine behind verify_tenant_range_chunks, and the
570	    # single validation body both the bytes and chunked offline range entries
571	    # delegate to: a segment is validated as a detached migration fragment --
572	    # the chain tail it continues is named by expected_prev, never by the
573	    # target log -- so no AuditChain path is ever probed. Every physical line
574	    # must be a record of the one declared canonical JSON tenant identity
575	    # carrying exactly the five FIELDS keys; seqs must run start_seq,
576	    # start_seq+1, ... with the first prev equal to expected_prev, and each
577	    # hash is recomputed with the existing algorithm. The mechanics are
578	    # _StreamScan's exactly: bytes accumulate behind LF-only physical-line
579	    # boundaries, strict UTF-8 decoding waits for the completed line, chunks
580	    # may be cut at any UTF-8/JSON/LF position, and the first defective
581	    # completed line stops feed so the caller never pulls another chunk.
582	    #
583	    # The first verdict is kept in _defect as a dict shaped exactly like the
584	    # public failure result ({ok: False, reason, at, tenant, start_seq,
585	    # end_seq}); a record of another canonical tenant identity violates the
586	    # single-tenant segment contract and is raised as _ForeignTenant (surfaced
587	    # as ValueError), the same rule the import scans use, and wins by
588	    # physical line order over a later chain defect. After all lines, an empty
589	    # segment or a declared end_seq the records stop short of is the missing
590	    # verdict "declared range missing its tail".
591	    def __init__(self, chain, tenant, start_seq, end_seq, expected_prev):
592	        self._chain = chain
593	        self.tenant = tenant
594	        self.start_seq = start_seq
595	        self.end_seq = end_seq
596	        self._key = chain._tenant_key(tenant)
597	        self._expected = start_seq
598	        self._prev = expected_prev
599	        self.count = 0
600	        self._buffer = b""
601	        self._line_no = 0
602	        self._defect = None
603	
604	    def feed(self, chunk):
605	        # Fold one bytes chunk into the running segment and validate every
606	        # physical line it completes, exactly the _StreamScan loop: a
607	        # completed line is checked the instant its LF arrives, so the first
608	        # defective line ends the scan and a chunked caller never requests
609	        # another chunk. Returns the kept verdict dict or None while valid.
610	        if self._defect is not None:
611	            return self._defect
612	        self._buffer += chunk
613	        while True:
614	            idx = self._buffer.find(b"\n")
615	            if idx < 0:
616	                return None
617	            line_bytes = self._buffer[:idx]
618	            self._buffer = self._buffer[idx + 1:]
619	            self._line_no += 1
620	            try:
621	                self._check_line(line_bytes)
622	            except _ForeignTenant:
623	                raise
624	            if self._defect is not None:
625	                return self._defect
626	
627	    def end(self):
628	        # Finalize the segment: the bytes pending after the last LF are the
629	        # final physical line (a segment need not end with LF), then the
630	        # declared interval must be covered exactly. Returns the kept verdict
631	        # dict or None when the segment fully verifies.
632	        if self._defect is not None:
633	            return self._defect
634	        if self._buffer:
635	            self._line_no += 1
636	            pending, self._buffer = self._buffer, b""
637	            self._check_line(pending)
638	            if self._defect is not None:
639	                return self._defect
640	        if self.count == 0:
641	            self._defect = self._fail("missing", self.start_seq)
642	            return self._defect
643	        if self.end_seq is not None and self._expected <= self.end_seq:
644	            # Records ran out before the declared closed interval: the first
645	            # seq the segment owes but does not contain locates the missing
646	            # tail.
647	            self._defect = self._fail("missing", self._expected)
648	            return self._defect
649	        return None
650	
651	    def _fail(self, reason, at):
652	        return {
653	            "ok": False,
654	            "reason": reason,
655	            "at": at,
656	            "tenant": self.tenant,
657	            "start_seq": self.start_seq,
658	            "end_seq": self.end_seq,
659	        }
660	
661	    def _check_line(self, line_bytes):
662	        # Validate one complete physical line with the exact strict rules the
663	        # import-range scan uses: strict UTF-8 then strict standard JSON
664	        # (duplicate keys and non-standard numbers rejected), a single object
665	        # of the declared canonical tenant identity carrying exactly the five
666	        # FIELDS keys, the expected JSON-integer seq, the predecessor digest
667	        # and a recomputed current hash. The first problem in physical order
668	        # decides and fills "at" the same way _scan_import_range's _Broken
669	        # does: the record's own plain-int seq for a missing-field line when
670	        # it carries one, else the expected seq; parse/object failures carry
671	        # the physical line number.
672	        try:
673	            raw = line_bytes.decode("utf-8")
674	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
675	            self._defect = self._fail("missing", self._line_no)
676	            return
677	        try:
678	            item = _strict_loads(raw)
679	        except Exception:
680	            self._defect = self._fail("missing", self._line_no)
681	            return
682	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:
683	            self._defect = self._fail("missing", self._line_no)
684	            return
685	        if self._chain._tenant_key(item["tenant"]) != self._key:
686	            raise _ForeignTenant(self._line_no)
687	        if set(item) != set(FIELDS):
688	            seq = item.get("seq")
689	            at = seq if isinstance(seq, int) and not isinstance(seq, bool) \
690	                else self._expected
691	            self._defect = self._fail("missing", at)
692	            return
693	        seq = item["seq"]
694	        # A declared closed interval must be covered exactly: once the
695	        # record for end_seq has verified, any further physical line sits
696	        # past the interval the fragment was declared to be and is a
697	        # sequence defect located at the first seq beyond it.
698	        if self.end_seq is not None and self._expected > self.end_seq:
699	            self._defect = self._fail("sequence", self._expected)
700	            return
701	        # Same strict JSON-integer seq rule as every other scan: a float
702	        # spelling (1.0, 1e0), bool, string, null, array/object or a
703	        # mismatching integer is a sequence defect, never renumbered.
704	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int) \
705	                or seq != self._expected:
706	            self._defect = self._fail("sequence", self._expected)
707	            return
708	        if item["prev"] != self._prev:
709	            self._defect = self._fail("digest", self._expected)
710	            return
711	        if item["hash"] != self._chain._hash(item):
712	            self._defect = self._fail("digest", self._expected)
713	            return
714	        self.count += 1
715	        self._prev = item["hash"]
716	        self._expected += 1
717	
718	    def result(self):
719	        # Project a fully verified segment into the public success shape:
720	        # start/end echo the declared interval (an open tail closes at the
721	        # actual last seq), count is the record count and hash the last
722	        # record's digest -- exactly the head assertion a subsequent
723	        # import_tenant_range call needs.
724	        return {
725	            "ok": True,
726	            "tenant": self.tenant,
727	            "start_seq": self.start_seq,
728	            "end_seq": (self.end_seq if self.end_seq is not None
729	                        else self.start_seq + self.count - 1),
730	            "count": self.count,
731	            "hash": self._prev,
732	        }

735	class AuditChain:
736	    def __init__(self, path):
737	        self.path = Path(path)
738	
739	    @contextlib.contextmanager
740	    def _dir_lease(self):
741	        # Auxiliary exclusive lease on the containing directory itself. It
742	        # never carries data bytes; its only job is to make the moment a data
743	        # file first appears indivisible relative to a conditional append
744	        # that is allowed to create the file only on its winning branch.
745	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
746	        dfd = os.open(self.path.parent, os.O_RDONLY)
747	        try:
748	            fcntl.flock(dfd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
749	            yield
750	        finally:
751	            fcntl.flock(dfd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
752	            os.close(dfd)
753	
754	    @contextlib.contextmanager
755	    def _write_lease(self):
756	        # Exclusive lease for one read-modify-append. The same open file
757	        # description carries the lock, the history read and the final append:
758	        # flock is tied to that description, so the lease cannot be silently
759	        # lost to a second open of the path, and the bytes appended are the
760	        # ones computed from the bytes just read. A fresh fd per call makes
761	        # flock genuinely exclude both other processes and other threads.
762	        # The creating open happens inside the directory lease, so a
763	        # conditional append probing a not-yet-existing path cannot race the
764	        # file's first appearance (see append_if_head); the lease is released
765	        # again before blocking on the data file, so it never serializes
766	        # unrelated chains in the same directory for a write's duration.
767	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
768	        with self._dir_lease():
769	            f = open(self.path, "a+b")
770	        try:
771	            fcntl.flock(f.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
772	            f.seek(0)
773	            yield f
774	            # Flush while the lease is still held, so the lock is released
775	            # only after the full record has reached the kernel file.
776	            f.flush()
777	        finally:

781	    def _read_snapshot(self):
782	        # One complete, self-consistent read-only view, protected by a shared
783	        # lease on the data file itself. The file is opened O_RDONLY, so a
784	        # verify never creates the path: when it does not exist yet that is a

787	        # state either before or after some append, never a partial record.

799	    @staticmethod
800	    def _split_lf(text):
801	        # Physical lines are bounded by exactly one character: the byte 0x0A
802	        # (LF), so a CRLF sequence is still one line -- the trailing CR stays
803	        # attached to its line and strict JSON accepts it as line-ending
804	        # whitespace. No other character ends a record: U+0085, U+2028,
805	        # U+2029 and a bare CR are valid UTF-8 content of the current line
806	        # and are handed to strict JSON (which keeps the three Unicode
807	        # separators as ordinary string content and rejects a raw CR inside
808	        # a JSON string). str.splitlines() must never be used here: it treats
809	        # all of those as line boundaries. The input is non-empty and, for a
810	        # trailing-LF text, the single empty segment after the final LF is
811	        # dropped (matching a physical record count: every LF terminates one
812	        # line, it does not begin an extra empty one).
813	        lines = text.split("\n")
814	        if text.endswith("\n"):
815	            lines.pop()

818	    @classmethod
819	    def _decode_lines(cls, data):
820	        # Split the raw JSONL bytes into LF-bounded physical lines while
821	        # treating the first illegal UTF-8 byte as a hard, locatable stop
822	        # point. Returns (lines, bad_line): lines are the complete physical
823	        # lines preceding any corruption (all lines when the bytes are valid
824	        # UTF-8), bad_line is the 1-based LF physical line number of the
825	        # first undecodable line or None. A bad line is never yielded, even
826	        # if the bytes before the illegal byte looked like complete JSON:
827	        # callers scan the preceding complete lines first, so an earlier
828	        # JSON/sequence/digest error still takes priority. Empty bytes are
829	        # zero physical lines, not one blank one.
830	        if not data:
831	            return [], None
832	        try:
833	            return cls._split_lf(data.decode("utf-8")), None
834	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
835	            # start is the offset of the first byte that cannot be decoded;
836	            # everything before it is a valid UTF-8 prefix. Physical lines
837	            # count LF bytes only, so the bad line's number is one plus the
838	            # number of LFs before that offset.
839	            start = exc.start
840	            bad_line = data.count(b"\n", 0, start) + 1
841	            cut = data.rfind(b"\n", 0, start) + 1  # start of the bad line
842	            prefix = data[:cut]
843	            lines = cls._split_lf(prefix.decode("utf-8")) if prefix else []
844	            return lines, bad_line
